subject: Preserve debug traces for production tokenization issue
messages:
From: Support Team <support@acme.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Preserve debug traces for production tokenization issue

Hi Evelyn,

We started seeing intermittent tokenization failures in our production calls to Redwood yesterday (errors show up as malformed tokens, sometimes causing partial responses). Our engineers believe the best way to debug the issue is to preserve a small set of recent request/response traces and the server-side KV/cache fragments tied to a handful of request IDs (we've attached an example audit_log_excerpt.csv with the request IDs).

I understand Redwood's default retention is 7 days for trace-level logs in our configuration, but this problem appears to require a 14-day retention window so our team and yours can reproduce and root-cause it; it may need multiple passes with different prompts. Can you advise what the process is to request a temporary retention exception and what safeguards/redaction Redwood requires for debug data that may contain customer PII or content?

We can sign any required short-form exception and provide a scoped list of request IDs and exact time windows. Appreciate quick guidance — we're blocked on a high-severity issue.

Thanks,
John Donohoe
Senior SRE, Acme Corp
john.donohoe@acme.com

Attachments: audit_log_excerpt.csv (CSV, 12KB)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: John Donohoe <support@acme.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Preserve debug traces for production tokenization issue

John — thanks for the quick heads-up and the sample log. I’m escalating this immediately to our security and compliance reviewers (cc'ed).

High-level plan I propose now:
- We will accept a scoped, timeboxed retention exception limited to the exact request IDs you provide.
- Security needs the data to be stored in an encrypted, access-controlled bucket with audit logging; they may require redaction of PII prior to any human review.
- Legal/compliance will need a signed short-form retention exception (I’ve attached the standard form below) and a statement of purpose and timeline.

Sergio / Maya — can you review the attached excerpt and advise whether we can authorize a 14-day retention for the listed traces, and what redaction/access controls must be applied? If you approve, I will send Acme the signed exception and open a temporary storage endpoint in our private S3 with MFA-backed access.

John — please reply with the final scoped list of IDs and a short justification for 14 days (if you can state why 7 is insufficient).

—Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
(Attachment: retention_exception_request.pdf)

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 12:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Preserve debug traces for production tokenization issue

Evelyn — reviewed the sample log and the initial ask. Quick notes: 

- Scope: We should limit to the explicit request IDs and the smallest possible window (+/- 5 minutes). Avoid bulk retention.
- Retention length: Security is comfortable with a temporary 14-day retention if: (1) data is stored encrypted with separate key material, (2) access is restricted to named Redwood engineers + explicit Acme SREs, and (3) each access is logged and reviewed.
- PII: Before any human viewing, we should run automated redaction for obvious PII (email addresses, phone numbers, SSNs). If redaction risks removing context needed to reproduce, we can allow constrained human review but only after approval from Legal and with an audit observer.
- Audit: We will generate an access report at the end of the retention period and auto-delete the object once the window expires.

I’ve attached my quick security notes (security_review_notes.txt) and included a checklist below we should complete prior to granting access.

Security checklist (to be completed):
- Signed retention_exception_request.pdf on file
- Signed access list with named users
- Automated PII redaction pass completed OR explicit approval for manual review
- Link to Jira incident (INF-4321) recorded in retention request

If Legal agrees, I approve the 14-day hold under those constraints.

—Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Security Lead — Redwood Inference
sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
(Attachment: security_review_notes.txt)

From: Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 15:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Preserve debug traces for production tokenization issue

Evelyn / Sergio — Legal/compliance quick take: we can approve a 14-calendar-day exception provided the following are in place before any human access: 
1) Scoped IDs and time windows are formalized in the retention request (customer-provided list).
2) Automated PII redaction run and results archived. If redaction materially prevents debugging, Acme must explicitly acknowledge and sign off for manual review.
3) A named access list for Redwood engineers and Acme SREs, with MFA required and justification for each name.
4) Auto-delete policy configured and monitored; an audit report delivered at deletion.

Operational note: for future incidents we should standardize a one-page short form so customers can sign quickly; I’ll draft it and link to the drive.

I’m comfortable with the 14-day window under the constraints above.

—Maya
Maya Srinivasan
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Compliance — Redwood Inference
maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: John Donohoe <support@acme.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 15:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Preserve debug traces for production tokenization issue

John — thanks for the extra details provided in your reply (we received the final list of request IDs and the short justification). Next steps and what we’ve authorized: 

1) Temporary exception granted: Redwood will retain the exact request traces you provided for 14 calendar days, starting 2026-11-15T16:00:00-08:00 and expiring 2026-11-29T16:00:00-08:00.
2) Controls in place: data will be encrypted with separate key material, stored in a restricted bucket, and access will be restricted to the named list (Redwood engineers: sergio_alvarez, ken_choi; Acme SREs: john.donohoe@acme.com). All access is logged and will be included in the deletion audit.
3) PII/redaction: we ran an automated redaction pass on the retained objects. If Acme requests manual review that requires unreduced context, we will need a signed manual-review acknowledgement (I’ve attached the retention_exception_request.pdf for signature).
4) Audit & deletion: an access report will be shared at deletion and the object will be auto-deleted at expiration.

Please sign the attached short-form retention exception and return it to retention-requests@redwood.ai. Once we have the signed form, we’ll send credentials to the two named Acme SREs and grant access to the retention bucket.

Apologies for the disruption — our infra team is prioritizing the tokenization reproduction with Acme. Sergio / Maya — flag me if any outstanding items need to be updated.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
(Attachments: retention_exception_request.pdf, audit_log_excerpt.csv)
